sketches: Both ask to characterize the finite families F of digraphs such that digraphs with no induced member of F have bounded dichromatic number ('heroic sets' = 'χ⃗-finite families').

Both ask to characterize the finite sets F of digraphs such that F-free (induced) digraphs have bounded dichromatic number: 'chi-vec-finite families' (Question 1.1 of arXiv:2306.04710) and 'heroic sets' (Problem 1.2 of arXiv:2009.13319) are the same notion by definition.

source.name: Heroic sets for bounded dichromatic number
source.statement: What are the finite sets $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs for which the class $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ has bounded dichromatic number?
source.context: This is the central problem of the paper, extending the Gyárfás-Sumner interrogation to directed graphs via the dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}$. A finite set $\mathcal{F}$ of digraphs is called heroic if $\mathrm{Forb}_{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathcal{F})$ has bounded dichromatic number. The paper focuses primarily on characterizing heroic sets of size three.

target.name: χ-finite families characterizing dichromatic boundedness
target.statement: Which finite families $F$ of digraphs are $\vec{\chi}$-finite?
target.context: A family $F$ is $\vec{\chi}$-finite if there is a constant $c$ such that all $F$-free digraphs have dichromatic number at most $c$. This is the overarching open question motivating the study of heroes in hereditary classes of digraphs, and all main results of the paper contribute to it.

sketches: The conjectured characterization of heroic triples {K2↔, H, F} (H a hero, F an oriented forest) is the restriction of the general problem of characterizing heroic finite sets to sets of this special form.

target.name: Heroic triple characterization via transitive tournaments
target.statement: Let $H$ be a hero and let $F$ be an oriented forest. The set $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2}, H, F\}$ is heroic if and only if: either $F$ is the disjoint union of oriented stars, or $H$ is a transitive tournament.
target.context: This is the main conjecture of the paper, a digraph analog of the Gyárfás-Sumner conjecture for oriented graphs. The 'only if' direction is proved in Section 6.1. The case where both conditions hold simultaneously (H a transitive tournament and F a disjoint union of oriented stars) is already settled by Chudnovsky, Scott and Seymour [6].

sketches: If η denotes the Hadwiger number, then by Kostochka–Thomason every graph satisfies η(G) ≥ cχ(G)/√log χ(G), so η(G) ≤ f(ω) forces χ(G) ≤ g(ω) for some g; hence η-boundedness of H-free graphs for every forest H implies Gyárfás–Sumner. Depends on η being the Hadwiger number in this record.

source.name: η-boundedness for H-free graphs
source.statement: For every forest $H$, there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\eta(G)\leq f(\omega(G))$.
source.context: Proposed as an analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture ($\chi$-boundedness) for $\eta$-boundedness: just as $H$-free graphs are conjectured to be $\chi$-bounded for every forest $H$, the authors conjecture the same for $\eta$-boundedness. The paper proves this conjecture for an assortment of special forests, including stars and paths $P_t$ with $t\leq 5$.

target.name: Graphs with a forbidden induced tree are chi-bounded
target.statement: Say that a family $ {\mathcal F} $ of graphs is $ \chi $ - bounded if there exists a function $ f: {\mathbb N} \rightarrow {\mathbb N} $ so that every $ G \in {\mathcal F} $ satisfies $ \chi(G) \le f (\omega(G)) $ . Conjecture For every fixed tree $ T $ , the family of graphs with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $ T $ is $ \chi $ -bounded.
target.context: This deep conjecture remains open despite considerable effort. Note that the conjecture would be false were the graph $ T $ to be permitted to contain a cycle, since then the class would admit graphs of high girth (where $ \omega = 2 $ ) and high chromatic number. It is an easy exercise to prove this conjecture in the special case when $ T $ is either a path or a star, but things get difficult from here. Kierstead and Penrice solved the special case when $ T $ has radius 2, and Kierstead and Zhu solved the special case when $ T $ has radius 3 and has the property that every vertex incident with the center vertex has degree 2. Scott proved that the class of graphs which exclude all subdivisions of a fixed tree $ T $ as induced subgraphs are $ \chi $ -bounded. It follows from this that Gyarfas's conjecture also holds for subdivisions of stars.

sketches: Problem __00 asks the maximum fractional chromatic number of d-degenerate K_r-free graphs; __04 is the specific assertion that this maximum is o_r(d) for each r ≥ 4, so determining the value in __00 resolves __04.

Both problems concern the same extremal quantity: Problem 4.1 asks to determine the maximum fractional chromatic number of K_r-free d-degenerate graphs, and Problem 6.4 asks only whether this maximum is o_r(d) for r ≥ 4; a full determination resolves the yes/no question.

source.name: Fractional chromatic number of K_r-free d-degenerate graphs
source.statement: What is the maximum fractional chromatic number of a $d$-degenerate, $K_{r}$-free graph?
source.context: Given the main theorem of Martinsson [26] on triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs and its many applications, the authors seek a generalization of Harris' conjecture for $K_{r}$-free graphs. One might guess the answer is $O_{r}\left(\frac{d\log\log d}{\log d}\right)$ by analogy with Johansson's bound for $K_r$-free graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$, but Theorem 1.6 shows this is not the case.

target.name: Sub-linear χ_f for K_r-free degenerate graphs
target.statement: Let $r\geq 4$. Is it true that the maximum fractional chromatic number of $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graphs is $o_{r}(d)$?
target.context: Theorem 1.6 gives a lower bound of $\Omega(d/\log^{(r-2)}d)$ on the fractional chromatic number of $K_r$-free $d$-degenerate graphs, which approaches linear in $d$ as $r$ increases, leaving open whether the maximum is truly sub-linear for each fixed $r\geq 4$.
